summary: Phase 6 (kst-lesser-holes_20260521 Phase 1 Quality) Red adversarial audit. The targeted vitest suite currently passes 20 files / 285 tests, but the contracts under test are under-specified: displayLevelSchema accepts empty/non-monotonic/duplicate-id bands, progressTrendHistorySchema accepts empty/out-of-order/duplicate-snapshot history, EDGE_ENDPOINT_RULES is duplicated across schemas.ts and validation.ts, transfers_to coverage lacks key negative cases and the zero-weight boundary, the public API contract test is shallow, and several test files carry stale Red-phase headers that misrepresent the live suite state. New Red tests have been authored to make these gaps fail the targeted command.

blocking_findings.title: displayLevelSchema accepts invalid display-level bands
blocking_findings.description: displayLevelSchema in packages/knowledge-space-core/src/level-projection.ts is currently z.array(displayLevelItemSchema) with no refinement. It accepts an empty band, duplicate level ids, and non-monotonic minMastery values. A valid display-level band must have at least one level, unique ids, and minMastery values that are non-decreasing so projectDisplayLevel can map monotonically.

blocking_findings.title: progressTrendHistorySchema accepts invalid history windows
blocking_findings.description: progressTrendHistorySchema in packages/knowledge-space-core/src/progress-trend.ts is currently z.array(masterySnapshotSchema) with no refinement. It accepts an empty history, out-of-order timestamps, and duplicate masteredNodeIds within a single snapshot. A valid history must be non-empty, chronologically ordered, and each snapshot must contain unique node ids.

blocking_findings.title: EDGE_ENDPOINT_RULES duplicated between schemas.ts and validation.ts
blocking_findings.description: The endpoint-pairing rules are defined independently in packages/knowledge-space-core/src/schemas.ts and packages/knowledge-space-core/src/validation.ts. Any future rule change must be applied in two places, guaranteeing drift. The rules should live in one canonical module imported by both consumers.

blocking_findings.title: transfers_to tests miss negative cases and weight boundary
blocking_findings.description: edge-type-transfers-to.test.ts covers same-domain rejection and basic cross-domain acceptance, but lacks explicit rejections for wrong source kind, wrong target kind, same-domain concept pairs, and lacks a positive acceptance test for zero-weight edges.

blocking_findings.title: public-api-contract.test.ts is shallow
blocking_findings.description: public-api-contract.test.ts only exercises type-level imports and basic parse acceptance. It does not import all named exports from root and subpaths, does not exercise projectDisplayLevel with a real instance, and does not assert the negative schema cases that prove the public API rejects invalid data.

blocking_findings.title: Stale Red-phase headers in passing test files
blocking_findings.description: Multiple kst-lesser-holes test files still carry headers claiming the tests are 'Red', 'expected to FAIL', or that the implementation 'does not yet include' features that are now live. These stale headers mislead readers and violate the test-strategy directive that passing files must not contain 'Status: RED' / 'expected to FAIL' / 'At HEAD ... missing' prose.

nonblocking_findings.title: LevelProjectionFn return type is under-specified
nonblocking_findings.description: LevelProjectionFn is currently typed as (state: KnowledgeState) => string. The return type should be constrained to a known level id so domain-supplied projections cannot return arbitrary strings. This is a type-level change; the runtime test exercises a real projection instance and verifies the returned id is a member of the supplied band.
